privacy.meta.description: What Markdown Plus processes, what it stores, and when it connects to other services. A clear guide to your data and privacy controls.

privacy.sections.scope.title: Scope
privacy.sections.scope.body1: This policy applies to the Markdown Plus Chrome extension. It explains what information the extension handles, where that information is stored, and when a network request may occur.
privacy.sections.information-processed-o: When you choose to open or edit a supported local document, Markdown Plus processes its content, file name, and local file URL or path in Chrome to provide viewing, navigation, editing, saving, printing, and export features. This processing happens locally in the browser. Document content is not sent to a server operated by the Markdown Plus developer.
privacy.sections.information-stored-by-t: Reader, editor, explorer, theme, and plugin preferences are stored in {code0} when available. Chrome may sync them through the Google account signed in to Chrome. If sync storage is unavailable, the extension uses {code1}. A failed sync write does not cause an automatic switch to local storage. The extension also keeps the last complete settings snapshot in {code2}, so it can display those settings while synchronized data is incomplete.

Custom theme descriptions, colors, and background image references may sync with preferences. Background image files you choose remain on the current device in browser IndexedDB and are not uploaded to the developer. Image files do not sync; you may need to choose a local image again on another device.
If recent-file history is enabled, local file URLs, file names, and last-opened times are stored only in {code0} on the current Chrome profile. Recent-file paths are not placed in sync storage.

When supported and after you select a file for saving, Chrome may allow the extension to retain a file handle in browser IndexedDB. This lets later saves target the same file. Chrome remains responsible for file-system permission prompts and controls.
privacy.sections.network-requests.title: Network requests
privacy.sections.network-requests.body1: Markdown Plus does not upload local document content to a developer-operated service. Some workflows can still make network requests:
privacy.sections.network-requests.body2: A document can reference remote images or other resources. Chrome may request those resources from the host named in the document, which can receive standard request information such as your IP address and browser headers.
privacy.sections.network-requests.body3: An exported HTML or Word-compatible document containing math may reference KaTeX CSS from {code0}. Opening that file while online may contact jsDelivr. The styles used to display math within the extension are bundled with it.
privacy.sections.network-requests.body4: External links are opened only when you choose to follow them.
privacy.sections.network-requests.body5: Those third-party services process requests under their own privacy policies. Markdown Plus does not receive data from those requests.
privacy.sections.sharing-and-sale.title: Sharing and sale
privacy.sections.sharing-and-sale.body1: Markdown Plus uses the information described in this policy only to provide its stated document-workspace features, in accordance with the Chrome Web Store User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements. The developer does not sell, rent, or use this information for advertising, credit decisions, or profiling, and does not receive document content, local history, file handles, or background images. Chrome may sync preferences through your Google account as described above.
privacy.sections.permissions.title: Permissions
privacy.sections.permissions.body1: {code0} lets the extension recognize, read, and display local files.
privacy.sections.permissions.body2: {code0} stores preferences and recent-file history as described above.
privacy.sections.permissions.body3: {code0} supports reading local documents and directory listings for the Files explorer.
privacy.sections.permissions.body4: {code0} saves HTML, Word-compatible documents, and Mermaid SVG/PNG exports. Editor Save writes only to the original file you explicitly connect; it does not download a fallback copy.
privacy.sections.your-controls.title: Your controls
privacy.sections.your-controls.body1: You can disable recent-file history and clear its entries in Markdown Plus settings. In Settings → Themes, saving a replacement background image or changing to a non-image background removes the previous image from this device after the theme is saved successfully. Deleting a custom theme removes its local background image. Resetting extension settings also clears the local theme-image store. If image cleanup fails, an unused image may remain until you clear the extension's site data or uninstall it. You can revoke file access in Chrome, clear the extension's site data, or uninstall the extension. Uninstalling removes extension-managed browser storage according to Chrome's behavior; your original documents and exported files remain wherever you saved them.
privacy.sections.this-website.title: This website
privacy.sections.this-website.body1: The developer does not add analytics, advertising, forms, or cookies to this website. The site saves only your light or dark theme choice in your browser’s local storage and does not send that choice to the developer. GitHub Pages hosts the site, so GitHub may process technical request data under the {a0Open}GitHub General Privacy Statement{a0Close}.
Material changes will be published on this page with an updated effective date. The repository history provides a public record of revisions.
privacy.sections.contact.title: Contact
privacy.sections.contact.body1: For privacy questions or support, open an issue in the {a0Open}Markdown Plus GitHub repository{a0Close}.

guide.troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
guide.quick-start.lead: Start here if you have never used the extension. Once a Markdown file opens in the reader, you can try everything else in this guide.
guide.quick-start.availability: Markdown Plus is available on Chrome Web Store. Install it, then enable file URL access to read documents on your computer.
guide.quick-start.install: Open the official Chrome Web Store listing above. Select {strong0Open}Add to Chrome{strong0Close}, then {strong1Open}Add extension{strong1Close}. Use {strong2Open}Chrome 116{strong2Close} or newer.
guide.quick-start.permission: Open {code0Open}chrome://extensions{code0Close} in the address bar, find Markdown Plus, select {strong0Open}Details{strong0Close}, then enable {strong1Open}Allow access to file URLs{strong1Close}. This lets the extension read local files you open.
guide.quick-start.open: Drag a local Markdown file into a Chrome tab, or use the Open file shortcut below. Supported direct entry points are {code0Open}.md{code0Close}, {code1Open}.markdown{code1Close}, {code2Open}.mdown{code2Close} and {code3Open}.mdc{code3Close}. {strong0Open}Reload{strong0Close} any tab that was open before granting access.
guide.quick-start.pin: Pin Markdown Plus from Chrome’s Extensions menu. Select its toolbar icon to open the popup, where {strong0Open}Reader, Editor, Plugins and Recent{strong0Close} group the everyday controls.
guide.quick-start.caption: Without file access, the popup shows a notice and a button to open Chrome’s extension details. Enable access there, then reload your local document.
guide.quick-start.shortcut: Open a local file in Chrome
guide.quick-start.practice.title: Try it: a small document, lots to explore
guide.quick-start.practice.body: Download {code0Open}markdown-plus-tour.md{code0Close}, save it on your computer and open it in Chrome. It includes headings, tasks, a table, code, an alert, a formula and a Mermaid diagram. Use it as you work through the next chapters. The example content is in English.
guide.workspace.lead: The document stays in the center. {strong0Open}Files{strong0Close} sits on the left; {strong1Open}Outline{strong1Close} and document actions sit on the right. Hide or resize the side panels when you want more reading space.
guide.workspace.caption: The current reader: Files on the left, your document in the center, and Outline with document actions on the right. Available actions depend on the file type and window width.
guide.workspace.folder.title: Open a folder as a workspace
guide.workspace.folder.body: In Files, choose {strong0Open}Open folder…{strong0Close}, select the folder containing your notes or project docs, and grant access when Chrome asks. Expand a folder and select a supported file. The workspace may need permission again after reopening Chrome.
guide.workspace.refresh: After adding, removing or renaming files, use {strong0Open}Refresh file list{strong0Close}. It rescans the tree; it does not reload the open document. Missing files? Check {code0Open}.gitignore{code0Close} exclusions and scan limits in {path0Open}All settings → Files & Workspace{path0Close}, then refresh.
guide.workspace.search.title: Find text in this document or across files
guide.workspace.search.availability: Available in Markdown Plus 1.0.1 on Chrome Web Store.
guide.workspace.search.document: Press {key0} + {key1} to find text in the reading surface. When the editor has focus, it keeps its own Find/Replace. Use Chrome’s menu for page-wide Find, including visible sidebar text; rows not currently mounted on the page are unavailable to browser Find.
guide.workspace.search.workspace: Choose the magnifier in {strong0Open}Files{strong0Close}, or press {key0} + {key1} + {key2}, to search supported text-file contents in the current folder/workspace. On macOS, use Control, not Command. No second folder selection is needed when Files already has a searchable scope. Only the tree area changes; the header stays in place. The active unsaved draft is included, along with nested files allowed by the current exclusions and scan limits.
guide.workspace.search.modes: Combine {strong0Open}Aa — Match case{strong0Close}, {strong1Open}ab — Match whole word{strong1Close} and {strong2Open}Á — Match diacritics{strong2Close}. Defaults ignore case, match substrings and distinguish accents. Turn off diacritic matching so {code0Open}hai{code0Close} can match {code1Open}hải{code1Close} and {code2Open}duong{code2Close} can match {code3Open}đường{code3Close}. Regular expressions are not supported.
guide.workspace.search.results: Typing waits 250 ms before searching across files; Enter in the query runs immediately. Previous results stay visible but cannot be opened while the search updates. Results are grouped by file with line numbers and short excerpts. Open a result to highlight its location while keeping focus in the list; use {key0}, or {key1} + {key2}, for the next/previous visible result. Hidden Markdown syntax can open a read-only source view. Yellow marks matches; orange marks the current match.
guide.workspace.search.refresh: Search temporarily keeps a limited amount of file content in memory for faster results. All matching happens on your device. {strong0Open}Search again{strong0Close} reads the latest contents of the files in the current list, while {strong1Open}Refresh file list{strong1Close} updates added, removed or renamed files. A folder opened as a snapshot must be selected again to read newer file contents. Search does not continuously watch every file or save a permanent content index.
guide.workspace.search.limits: Files over {strong0Open}2 MiB{strong0Close}, searches reaching {strong1Open}2,000 matches{strong1Close}, and searches reaching a {strong2Open}15-second processing budget{strong2Close} can leave results incomplete. Read the partial-result notice, narrow the query or refresh as appropriate. Images are not searched.
guide.workspace.outline: Select a heading in {strong0Open}Outline{strong0Close} to jump to that part of the document. Headings come from your Markdown source. In a narrow window, look in the document actions {strong1Open}overflow menu{strong1Close} for commands that no longer fit.
guide.workspace.direct: Directly in Chrome, or through Files.
guide.workspace.viaFiles: Open a Markdown file first, then select the file in Files.
guide.workspace.imageTypes: PNG, JPG/JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, ICO, APNG and SVG. Open through Files.
guide.reader.lead: Open the popup → {strong0Open}Reader{strong0Close}. Start with a theme, then adjust the text and page width until a long paragraph is easy to read. These preferences apply across your documents.
guide.reader.caption: Reader includes Theme, Font family, Font size, Line height and Content width. All settings sits at the bottom. Wait for Settings saved before closing the popup.
guide.reader.type.title: Text that suits you
guide.reader.type.body: Choose a font family, font size from {strong0Open}12–28 px{strong0Close}, and line height from {strong1Open}1.2–2.2{strong1Close}. Font presets use fonts installed on your computer, with fallback fonts if a preset is unavailable.
guide.reader.layout.title: Room for the document
guide.reader.layout.body: Set content width from {strong0Open}640–1400 px{strong0Close} and choose whether to {strong1Open}Show table of contents{strong1Close}. In {strong2Open}General{strong2Close} settings, you can hide document statistics or change scrollbar visibility. Statistics include words, characters with spaces and estimated reading time.
guide.reader.reset: Need a fresh start? {strong0Open}Reset reader UI{strong0Close} restores the default theme selection, typography and layout. To change the interface language, go to {path0Open}All settings → General → Interface language{path0Close}. Document text is never translated.
guide.rich-markdown.lead: Markdown Plus goes beyond headings and paragraphs. Open the practice file, then try these features. All registered plugins are enabled by default; manage them in popup → {strong0Open}Plugins{strong0Close}.
guide.rich-markdown.code.title: Code & tables
guide.rich-markdown.code.body: Fenced code blocks support syntax highlighting and a copy control. Tables get a more readable presentation. Add a language after the opening code fence, such as {code0Open}javascript{code0Close}, for the matching code grammar.
guide.rich-markdown.notes.title: Notes & references
guide.rich-markdown.notes.body: Use GitHub-style alerts, footnotes, emoji and heading anchors in your notes. Task lists are displayed as {strong0Open}read-only{strong0Close} checkboxes: change the Markdown source to check or uncheck an item.
guide.rich-markdown.math.title: Math & colors
guide.rich-markdown.math.body: {strong0Open}KaTeX{strong0Close} renders inline and block formulas. {strong1Open}Color preview{strong1Close} adds swatches for supported color values; open a swatch to copy {code0Open}HEX{code0Close}, {code1Open}RGB{code1Close} or {code2Open}HSL{code2Close}. Plugin switches let you turn each feature on or off.
guide.rich-markdown.practice: Try it in the practice file: jump to “{strong0Open}A diagram{strong0Close}”, copy the JavaScript block, then find the formula and the {code0Open}#2563eb{code0Close} color value. If something appears as raw text, check the corresponding plugin switch.
guide.diagrams.lead: A Mermaid code block becomes a diagram when the plugin is enabled. You can also open a standalone {code0Open}.mermaid{code0Close} file through Files and switch between the rendered diagram and its source.
guide.diagrams.open: Open a diagram or image in the larger viewer. Use fit, zoom and pan to inspect details; close the viewer to return to your document.
guide.diagrams.export: For Mermaid, copy the source or export {strong0Open}SVG{strong0Close} or {strong1Open}PNG{strong1Close}. PNG export offers {strong2Open}1×–4×{strong2Close} scales. Use SVG for vector artwork, or a larger PNG scale when you need more pixels.
guide.diagrams.renderer: In {path0Open}popup → Plugins{path0Close}, choose {strong0Open}Official{strong0Close} for the broadest Mermaid syntax support, or try {strong1Open}Beautiful{strong1Close} for an alternative layout. If a diagram fails with Beautiful, switch to Official and check the source syntax.
guide.themes.lead: Choose a built-in theme from {path0Open}popup → Reader → Theme{path0Close}, or {path1Open}All settings → Themes → Active reader theme{path1Close}. Light, dark, high-contrast and colorful options share the same reader controls.
guide.themes.caption: Themes lets you select the active reader theme or start Add custom theme. Saved custom themes appear in your library.
guide.themes.create.title: Create a custom theme
guide.themes.create.name: Choose {strong0Open}Add custom theme{strong0Close}, give it a name and select a {strong1Open}Base theme{strong1Close}. Changing the base resets the draft color palette, so choose it first.
guide.themes.create.colors: Adjust page, document, panel, text, heading, link and code colors. Check the {strong0Open}live preview{strong0Close} as you go, including the contrast of secondary text.
guide.themes.create.syntax: Under {strong0Open}Code highlighting{strong0Close}, follow the base theme or choose a bundled syntax theme. This changes rendered code colors, independently of the editor’s content.
guide.themes.create.background: Choose a background, adjust its fit and dimming if needed, then select {strong0Open}Create theme{strong0Close} or {strong1Open}Save changes{strong1Close}. Draft changes are not saved until you confirm.
guide.themes.editor.caption: The theme editor has identity, colors, code highlighting and background sections, with a live preview on the right. Create theme sits at the bottom.
guide.themes.background.title: Choose your background
guide.themes.background.body: Keep the theme color, choose a solid scene, make a two-color gradient, or add a local PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, GIF or APNG up to {strong0Open}5 MiB{strong0Close}. Image controls include fit, position and repeat. Use Dimming to keep the document readable.
guide.themes.background.motion: Motion offers {strong0Open}Follow system{strong0Close}, {strong1Open}Animate{strong1Close} and {strong2Open}Still{strong2Close}. Follow system respects reduced-motion preferences. Still hides an animated image background rather than freezing a frame.
guide.themes.background.local: Background images stay on this device. {strong0Open}They do not sync with Chrome{strong0Close} and are excluded from settings JSON backups. Keep the original images and choose them again on another device.
guide.updates.lead: Editing in another app? Markdown Plus can detect a saved revision of the active document. Set your preferred behavior in {path0Open}All settings → General → Document updates{path0Close}.
guide.updates.ask.body: Checks for changes and waits for you to load the update. Choose this when you want to review before replacing the article.
guide.updates.auto.body: Loads the saved file once it stops changing and you stop interacting, while trying to preserve your reading position.
guide.updates.off.body: Stops automatic checks. You can still use {strong0Open}Check now{strong0Close} for a one-time check.
guide.updates.steps: Use {strong0Open}Document updates{strong0Close} in the viewer to check or load a revision. When a comparison is available, choose {strong1Open}View changes{strong1Close} to see added and removed source lines. Markdown comparisons also show affected sections; images update without a source comparison.
guide.updates.review: An open comparison stays on the selected revision until you choose {strong0Open}Review latest{strong0Close}. {strong1Open}Automatic{strong1Close} mode can still update the article behind the comparison. Use {strong2Open}Ask{strong2Close} when you want control over when updates load.
guide.updates.limits: Checks run while the tab is visible and support files up to {strong0Open}5 MiB{strong0Close}. {strong1Open}Only the active document{strong1Close} is checked, not the whole workspace or its linked images. A folder opened as a snapshot cannot be reread live; select it again for a fresh snapshot.
guide.editor.lead: The editor is {strong0Open}off by default{strong0Close}. It lets you edit Markdown beside a live preview and save to an explicitly verified local file.
guide.editor.enable: In {path0Open}popup → Editor{path0Close}, turn on Enable editor. Open a Markdown document, then choose {strong0Open}Edit Markdown{strong0Close} in the document actions.
guide.editor.connect: When prompted, select the {strong0Open}exact original file{strong0Close}. Check both its {strong1Open}folder and filename{strong1Close} before granting write access. The extension needs this connection to save back to the original.
guide.editor.edit: Edit with the live preview, or use {strong0Open}focus mode{strong0Close} to hide the preview. {strong1Open}Search and replace{strong1Close} is available. Popup → Editor also controls font size, tab size, word wrap and line numbers.
guide.editor.save: Choose {strong0Open}Save{strong0Close} or use {kbd0Open}Ctrl{kbd0Close} + {kbd1Open}S{kbd1Close} / {kbd2Open}⌘{kbd2Close} + {kbd3Open}S{kbd3Close}. Confirm the saved status before leaving. {strong1Open}Exit edit mode{strong1Close} before printing or exporting the document.
guide.editor.safety: If another app changes the file after editing begins, Save {strong0Open}refuses to overwrite{strong0Close} it. Your draft is never automatically replaced by document updates. Loading an external revision closes edit mode and asks for confirmation; {strong1Open}unsaved changes will be discarded{strong1Close}. Copy a draft you want to keep before loading that revision.
guide.export.lead: Use the document actions to take a readable copy elsewhere. Extra commands move into the {strong0Open}overflow menu{strong0Close} when the window is narrow.
guide.export.pdf.title: Print or save a PDF
guide.export.pdf.body: Choose {strong0Open}Print / Save as PDF{strong0Close}. In Chrome’s print dialog, choose your printer or Save as PDF, then check the preview and page settings before saving.
guide.export.document.title: Export Markdown
guide.export.document.body: For Markdown, choose {strong0Open}Export HTML{strong0Close} or {strong1Open}Export Word (.doc){strong1Close}. Depending on available space, these appear in {strong2Open}Export document{strong2Close} or the overflow menu. The .doc file is Word-compatible; diagram SVG/PNG exports use the diagram’s own menu.
guide.export.note: {strong0Open}Exit edit mode first{strong0Close}. Documents are processed locally, but remote resources referenced by a document can contact their hosts. Some exported HTML resources may use a CDN; see the privacy policy for details.
guide.settings.lead: Open popup → {strong0Open}All settings{strong0Close} for the full configuration. Most switches and selections save immediately; numeric limits use {strong1Open}Save changes{strong1Close} and theme drafts have their own save action. Always check the status message.
guide.settings.general: {strong0Open}General{strong0Close}: language, activation, scrollbars, document statistics, update mode and file URL access status. Chrome’s extension {strong1Open}Details{strong1Close} page controls the permission itself.
guide.settings.files: {strong0Open}Files & Workspace{strong0Close}: hierarchy guides, {code0Open}.gitignore{code0Close} exclusions, workspace restoration and scan limits. {strong1Open}Depth 0{strong1Close} scans only the selected root. Scan changes take effect on the next scan or refresh.
guide.settings.history: {strong0Open}Privacy & Data{strong0Close}: enable recent-file history, change how many entries are retained or clear the list. Popup → {strong1Open}Recent{strong1Close} reopens local Markdown files. Clearing this history {strong2Open}does not delete your files{strong2Close}.
guide.settings.advanced: {strong0Open}Advanced{strong0Close}: set the viewing size limit for standalone TXT, SQL, DBML and Mermaid files. It applies on the next open and {strong1Open}does not apply to Markdown{strong1Close}. This is separate from the {strong2Open}5 MiB{strong2Close} document-update limit.
guide.settings.about: {strong0Open}About{strong0Close}: find the installed version, compatibility details and support links. Include the version when reporting a problem.
guide.settings.caption: General includes Interface language, Document updates and File URL access. This page shows permission status; you grant access in Chrome’s extension details.
guide.settings.backup.title: Back up your preferences
guide.settings.backup.body: In Advanced, choose {strong0Open}Export JSON{strong0Close}. To restore a backup, use {strong1Open}Choose JSON{strong1Close} under {strong2Open}Import settings{strong2Close}; the file is validated before saving. Backups include preferences and custom-theme definitions, but {strong3Open}exclude documents, recent-file history and background images{strong3Close}.
guide.settings.backup.caption: Advanced includes Export JSON, Import settings and Reset all settings. Keep original background images separately; JSON backups exclude them.
guide.settings.reset: {strong0Open}Reset all settings{strong0Close} restores preferences and {strong1Open}removes custom themes and their stored backgrounds{strong1Close}. Section resets restore that section’s defaults. Recent-file history is cleared separately in Privacy & Data or Recent.
guide.settings.local: Your documents are processed in your browser {strong0Open}without a developer-operated upload service{strong0Close}. Preferences may sync through Chrome; recent paths, editor file connections and background images stay on the device. Changing the website theme only changes this website.
guide.troubleshooting.plain.question: My Markdown still opens as plain text.
guide.troubleshooting.plain.answer: Enable {strong0Open}Allow access to file URLs{strong0Close} in Chrome → Extensions → Markdown Plus → Details. Check {path0Open}All settings → General → Enable Markdown Plus{path0Close}, verify the .md/.markdown/.mdown/.mdc extension, then reload the tab.
guide.troubleshooting.formats.question: Can I use it on a website or open SQL directly?
guide.troubleshooting.formats.answer: The extension activates on local Markdown files. Download a remote Markdown file and open the local copy. For SQL, DBML, text, Mermaid and images, {strong0Open}first open Markdown{strong0Close}, then use Files to select the other document.
guide.troubleshooting.missing.question: Files are missing from the tree.
guide.troubleshooting.missing.answer: Check {code0Open}.gitignore{code0Close} and scan depth/file/folder limits in {strong0Open}Files & Workspace{strong0Close}, then choose {strong1Open}Refresh file list{strong1Close}. Grant folder access again if requested. A recent file that moved must be reopened from its new location.
guide.troubleshooting.stale.question: I saved elsewhere, but the document looks unchanged.
guide.troubleshooting.stale.answer: Use {path0Open}Document updates → Check now{path0Close} and load the update in Ask mode. Keep the tab visible and check the {strong0Open}5 MiB{strong0Close} limit. {strong1Open}Refresh file list{strong1Close} only updates the tree. For a snapshot workspace, select the folder again.
guide.troubleshooting.save.question: Editor Save reports a conflict.
guide.troubleshooting.save.answer: Another app changed the original file after editing began. {strong0Open}Copy any draft you want to keep{strong0Close}, then review the disk revision and reopen the correct file. Save will not force an overwrite. Check write permission if Chrome reports an access error.
guide.troubleshooting.background.questio: My background is missing on another device.
guide.troubleshooting.background.answer: Background images {strong0Open}do not sync{strong0Close} and are excluded from JSON backups. Edit the custom theme on that device, choose the original image again and save the theme.
guide.troubleshooting.settings.question: A setting will not save.
guide.troubleshooting.settings.answer: Read the {strong0Open}save status{strong0Close} for the specific error. Retry after a moment if changes were too frequent. If Chrome reports full settings storage, reduce custom-theme data or remove unused themes, then retry.
guide.troubleshooting.support: Still stuck? Include your Chrome version, extension version, the steps you tried and a small example with private content removed when opening an issue.
guide.end.title: Ready for your own documents.
guide.end.body: Open a local Markdown file, choose your favorite theme, and keep this guide nearby for the next feature you want to try.
guide.workspace.sourceFormats: TXT is shown as plain text. SQL and DBML can use syntax highlighting; DBML is a source viewer, not a database diagram generator. These formats are {strong0Open}read-only{strong0Close} here. Standalone Mermaid adds a diagram/source view; Markdown remains the format with Outline, experimental editing and document export.
guide.diagrams.resolution: In Mermaid and SVG zoom views, {strong0Open}Resolution{strong0Close} changes bitmap detail separately from zoom. Reveal its minus/plus controls by hovering, focusing or tapping the control. Levels increase in 0.25 steps from 1× up to {strong1Open}8×{strong1Close}, bounded by the image’s size and memory limits. {strong2Open}Maximum{strong2Close} means this image cannot go higher. This only affects the open preview, not the source or exported file.
guide.reader.navigation: Use {strong0Open}Back to top{strong0Close} to return to the beginning of a long document. Outline links navigate within the file; they do not change its source. Adjusting reader preferences changes the presentation, not the Markdown you saved.
guide.rich-markdown.caption: Code, tasks, a GitHub alert, math and a color swatch in the actual reader. Example document content stays in English.
guide.rich-markdown.plugins.caption: The top of Plugins includes code highlighting, task lists, heading anchors, tables and emoji.
guide.plugins.title: Choose the features you use
guide.diagrams.caption: Mermaid renders the document’s code as a diagram. Its toolbar offers source copying, a larger view, and SVG/PNG export.
guide.diagrams.zoom.caption: The larger viewer has Resolution, zoom, re-center and close controls at the top, with mouse and keyboard hints at the bottom.
guide.workspace.map.title: A quick map of the reader
guide.updates.caption: Document updates shows the current mode and a Check now button at the upper right.
guide.updates.review.caption: View changes marks added lines in green and removed lines in red, with affected sections listed on the left.
guide.editor.connect.caption: Select the exact original file before editing. Check the path shown in the dialog to avoid choosing a same-name copy.
guide.editor.caption: Edit Markdown on the left and see the preview on the right. The bottom status bar shows the cursor position, save status and connected save target.
guide.export.caption: When the action bar runs out of room, the overflow menu includes Print / Save as PDF, Export HTML and Export Word (.doc).
guide.troubleshooting.caption: When access is missing, File URL access reports that it is not allowed. Follow the instructions here to open Chrome’s extension details and enable it.
guide.rich-markdown.pluginsMore.caption: Scroll down for GitHub Alerts, Color preview, Math (KaTeX) and Mermaid, with the Official/Beautiful renderer choice at the bottom.
releases.meta.title: Release notes · Markdown Plus
releases.meta.description: What is included in Markdown Plus releases, how to get started, and known limitations.
releases.title: Release notes
releases.description: Version changes, release status, setup essentials, and known limitations.
releases.version.title: 1.0.0 — First Store release
releases.version.summary: A local Markdown workspace for reading, browsing, editing, and exporting in Chrome.
releases.features.read: Read local Markdown with an outline, highlighted code, tables, task lists, math, footnotes, GitHub-style alerts, and Mermaid diagrams.
releases.features.files: Browse folders and related Markdown, text, SQL, DBML, Mermaid, and image files in Files.
releases.features.themes: Choose light, dark, or custom themes; adjust typography and add a device-local background image.
releases.features.updates: Follow external edits with Ask, Automatic, or Off update modes and review source changes.
releases.features.editor: Opt in to the experimental Markdown editor with live preview and save to an explicitly connected original file.
releases.features.export: Export Markdown as HTML or Word-compatible .doc, export Mermaid as SVG/PNG, or print supported documents and save PDF through Chrome.
releases.features.languages: Use the interface in English, Vietnamese, or Simplified Chinese.
releases.setup.title: Getting started
releases.setup.summary: Chrome 116 or newer and one-time local file access.
releases.setup.body: Install from Chrome Web Store. In Chrome’s extension Details, enable Allow access to file URLs, then open or reload a local .md, .markdown, .mdown, or .mdc file. Other supported formats open through Files once the Markdown viewer is active.
releases.limitations.title: Known limitations
releases.limitations.summary: Experimental editing, local images, and export details.
releases.limitations.editor: Editing is experimental and off by default. Select and verify the original file and grant write permission before saving. Failed saves keep the draft and do not download a replacement copy.
releases.limitations.images: Custom background-image files stay on the device and are excluded from JSON backups. Choose the image again on another device.
releases.limitations.export: Math in HTML/Word exports may need external CSS/fonts, so offline rendering can differ. Word-compatible .doc is not native DOCX.
releases.limitations.updates: Live document updates check the visible active document and support files up to 5 MiB. Snapshot-only workspaces may need to be selected again.
releases.privacy: Documents are processed locally without a developer-operated upload service. Preferences may sync through Chrome. Referenced remote resources and exported Math can contact third-party hosts.
releases.revision.title: 1.0.0.1 — Change review scrolling fix
releases.revision.summary: A small bug-fix revision that keeps change review scrolling and long section lists contained.
releases.revision.scroll: Keep the change review dialog in view when scrolling over the area outside it.
releases.revision.sections: Scroll the affected-section list independently so long lists do not push the keyboard hint out of view or overflow the comparison layout.
releases.revision.displayVersion: Display the clean version 1.0.0.1 without a build timestamp.
releases.current.title: 1.0.1 — Search and more interface languages
releases.current.summary: Released November 10, 2026 on Chrome Web Store.
releases.current.languages: Add Spanish, German, Japanese, and Romanian across Settings, Popup, Viewer controls, and editor/search labels.
releases.current.website: Matching website pages, translated privacy policies, and Chrome Web Store descriptions are available.
releases.current.links: Open the website and privacy policy from About in the selected interface language.
releases.current.search: Find in the reading surface and search text files across the current workspace, including the active draft, with case, whole-word, and diacritic matching.
